newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuelan gasoline hike unlikely in first quarter.
newsitem.headline: Venezuelan gasoline hike unlikely in first quarter.

text.p: The Venezuelan government is unlikely to raise gasoline prices in the first quarter, state-run Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA) President Luis Giusti said.

Before taking such a decision, certain to be unpopular, the government has "a myriad of social and political problems to solve", he said, citing a prolonged labor strife and attempts to reform the outdated social security system.

Press reports last week said the government was mulling a possible 10-bolivar ($0.02), or 17 percent, gasoline price increase, to compensate rising production costs due to over 100 percent inflation last year.
An economic adjustment program agreed with the International Monetary Fund signed in July calls for such an increase in the second quarter of 1997.
Giusti said any increase after March 31 "is not a purely technical matter but would also carry political connotations."
Gasoline prices were last increased fivefold on April 15 last year but, in dollar terms, remain among the cheapest in the world.
